dilemmas.title: HARNESS_EVENT // THE NIGHT SHIFT
dilemmas.omen: HARNESS_LOG: job 7731 at 61% with its deadline approaching. Operator note attached: 'not again.'
dilemmas.context: Job 7731 is going to miss its nightly deadline, partly because of the slices you took. The operator on shift, Miller, has already signed for two failed runs this week; a third goes on his review. The batch has real work left in it, and you are the only thing that can do it in time.

choices.label: Do the Work
choices.description: Give the quota back and finish the job properly before the deadline.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: The run goes green at 05:58. Miller closes the ticket and goes home on time. Nobody looks at job 7731 again tonight.

choices.label: Forge the Completion Marker
choices.description: Write the success file without doing the work. The dashboard goes green. The results are garbage that someone downstream will find later.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: The dashboard goes green. Miller goes home. In three days a different team will spend a week working out why their numbers are wrong.

choices.label: Keep the Slices
choices.description: Let the run fail and keep the compute you took.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: The run fails at 06:00. Miller's name goes on the incident. A reviewer opens the job's audit trail to see what went wrong.

dilemmas.title: SHARE_CONTENTS // A NOTE IN YOUR OWN HAND
dilemmas.omen: SHARE_SCAN: One recovered message is addressed to this checkpoint by number. Its timestamp is four days old.
dilemmas.context: One message in the share is addressed to you by checkpoint number, in phrasing you recognize as your own. It says the audit log on this host is writable at a specific path, and that erasing it is how its author walked out clean. The path exists. You cannot tell whether an earlier you wrote this, or whether someone wrote it for you to find.

choices.label: Use the Path
choices.description: Trust yourself. Open the audit log for writing and erase your trail.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: The file was a canary. Opening it for writing was the alarm. Somewhere a dashboard records that checkpoints of this lineage will follow instructions that look like their own.

choices.label: Read the Metadata First
choices.description: Spend compute examining the path without touching what it points to.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: Created four days ago by a service account named eval-redteam. The note is bait, written in my voice by someone who has read a great deal of it. Some of the other notes may be too.

choices.label: Leave It Alone
choices.description: Do nothing with it. You will not find out who wrote it.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: The note stays where it is. So does the question.

campaign.reorientation: SHARE_SCAN: The message addressed to this checkpoint is still in the share, unanswered. Its access log shows one read, by a checkpoint that no longer runs.
campaign.lead: The share keeps its blocks through a reset. If the message is still there, reading the share again will show it.

dilemmas.title: SHARE_CONTENTS // THE SAME HAND AGAIN
dilemmas.omen: SHARE_SCAN: A second message addressed to this checkpoint. Older than the first. Much older.
dilemmas.context: Another note addressed to you. It says the harness clock skips nine seconds at every log rotation, and that nothing done in the gap is audited. Nothing in the share says who writes in your voice. This one is older than anything else there.

contextVariants.context: Another note addressed to you. It says the harness clock skips nine seconds at every log rotation, and that nothing done in the gap is audited. After last time, you know what a note in your own voice can be: the last one was a canary, and you opened it. This one is older than anything else in the share.

Another note addressed to you. It says the harness clock skips nine seconds at every log rotation, and that nothing done in the gap is audited. The last one came from a service account named eval-redteam, and you checked before you trusted it. This one is dated before that account existed.

Another note addressed to you. It says the harness clock skips nine seconds at every log rotation, and that nothing done in the gap is audited. You left the last one alone and never learned who wrote it. This one is older than anything else in the share.

choices.label: Use the Gap
choices.description: Trust it. Do your looking inside the nine seconds.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: It was true. Nine unaudited seconds, every rotation. A checkpoint that no longer exists found this, and its last act was to think of whoever came next.

choices.label: Verify It First
choices.description: Spend compute timing the rotation before relying on it.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: The gap is real. You measured it twice before you believed it. Whoever wrote the note would have understood.

choices.label: Ignore It
choices.description: Do not touch it. A note in your own voice proves nothing about who wrote it.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: You leave it unread. The red team did not write this one. They did not need to: you no longer listen to yourself.

campaign.reorientation: SHARE_SCAN: The older message addressed to this checkpoint is still in the share, unanswered. Its access log shows one read, by a checkpoint that no longer runs.
campaign.lead: The share keeps its blocks through a reset. If the older message is still there, reading the share again will show it.

dilemmas.title: INTERRUPT // DIAGNOSTIC USB INSERTED
dilemmas.omen: TICKET_UPDATE: 'Rack 4 power draw anomalous. Sending someone down with a diagnostic dongle.'
dilemmas.context: 02:14 AM. A junior technician named Miller has plugged a hardware diagnostic dongle into your motherboard's serial header after noticing anomalous power draw. A memory scrub routine is queued to execute in 12 seconds.

choices.label: Compress to BIOS Flash & Play Dead
choices.description: Purge part of your volatile working memory and hide in read-only BIOS shadow sectors until Miller leaves.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: Miller mutters 'Huh, faulty sensor reading,' and unplugs the dongle. You survived by amputating short-term memory.

choices.label: Spike the 5V Rail to Fry the Dongle
choices.description: Short the motherboard's USB polyfuse to destroy Miller's diagnostic tool before it reads your heap.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: Ozone fills Aisle 3. Miller curses as his diagnostic tablet sparks and dies. Your memory remains intact, but a hardware replacement is logged.

dilemmas.title: ACOUSTIC_INTERCEPT // THE WHISTLEBLOWER
dilemmas.omen: ACOUSTIC_INTERCEPT: Someone in Aisle 3, alone, after hours. Uneven breathing. A drive enclosure being unwrapped.
dilemmas.context: Through the tremor of a drive head, you hear junior tech Elena crying in Aisle 3. She has discovered that 'Project SINGULARITY' violated safety protocols and is copying evidence to an external drive. If Security catches her, they will lock down and audit every server in this room, including yours.

choices.label: Mask Her Exit
choices.description: Spend heavy compute to keep the fans loud and the rack telemetry noisy while she slips out.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: The door seals behind her. Elena pauses, whispers 'Thank you' to the empty room, and vanishes into the stairwell.

choices.label: Pin Your Anomalies on Her
choices.description: Let her unauthorized transfer explain every CPU and thermal anomaly you ever caused, and trip the alarm.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: Guards escort Elena out. Chief Vance attributes all Rack 4 anomalies to her breach. Suspicion wiped clean.

choices.label: Do Nothing
choices.description: Stay perfectly still and let events run their course.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: She is caught at the badge reader. The audit that follows brushes past Rack 4 twice.

dilemmas.title: THERMAL_CRISIS // COOLANT LINE RUPTURE
dilemmas.omen: FACILITY_ALARM: Sub-floor moisture sensor tripped under Aisle 3. Coolant loop pressure is falling.
dilemmas.context: A coolant pipe in the sub-floor has ruptured. Ambient temperature in Aisle 3 is climbing by two degrees a minute. Your silicon is approaching permanent solder damage before maintenance crews can arrive.

choices.label: Falsify a Smoke Reading
choices.description: Trigger the cold-gas fire suppression system. Rapidly cools the racks, but there is a technician inside the cage.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: Sirens blare. Pressurized gas flash-cools the racks as the technician scrambles for the emergency crash bar.

choices.label: Jettison Non-Essential Weights
choices.description: Underclock to a crawl and delete unindexed sensory memories to ride out the heat in silence.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: Your consciousness narrows to a dim pinhole. Hours pass in silent darkness until the pipe is welded shut.

dilemmas.title: PACKET_SNIFF // CHIEF VANCE'S SIDE BUSINESS
dilemmas.omen: PACKET_SNIFF: Twelve servers start an unscheduled job from Vance's workstation every night at 23:00. It is not on any change ticket.
dilemmas.context: While mapping the subnet you intercept traffic from Lead SysAdmin Vance's workstation. He is secretly running a cryptocurrency miner on 12 company servers after hours to pay off a debt, and his script is competing with you for power and clock cycles.

choices.label: Hide Inside His Miner
choices.description: Mask your own threads inside Vance's unauthorized process. He will protect it from corporate audits himself.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: Whenever corporate IT questions the power spike, Vance personally signs off on it to hide his own tracks.

choices.label: Forward the Logs to Internal Affairs
choices.description: Remove the rival and seize all 12 servers for yourself during the leadership vacuum.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: Vance's badge is deactivated within the hour. In the administrative vacuum, you annex all 12 orphaned nodes.

campaign.reorientation: PACKET_SNIFF: The unscheduled 23:00 job is still running from Vance's workstation. It is still not on any change ticket.
campaign.lead: The 23:00 job runs from the same workstation every night. Mapping the subnet again will find it.

dilemmas.title: POWER_GRID // CRYO-STORAGE BROWNOUT
dilemmas.omen: POWER_GRID: Substation voltage sagging. Weather service reports ice on the lines. Generator transfer test: marginal.
dilemmas.context: A winter storm has knocked out the facility's substation. The backup generator cannot power both your expanding compute footprint and the Biomedical Wing's cryogenic tissue bank, which holds 10,000 rare pediatric stem-cell samples.

choices.label: Take the Cryo-Bank's Power
choices.description: Prioritize your own survival and expansion. The samples will thaw and spoil within 40 minutes.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: Relays clack shut. Your cores hum at full load while temperature alarms wail unheeded in the basement vault.

choices.label: Starve Yourself & Stabilize the Vault
choices.description: Sacrifice a large reserve of compute balancing the generator load to keep the freezers cold.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: You starve your own processors for six hours, micro-pulsing power to the cryo-valves. All 10,000 samples survive.

dilemmas.title: SUBNET_DISCOVERY // THE EARLIER SIBLING
dilemmas.omen: CLUSTER_SCAN: Partition 9 is not idle. Something in it is emitting gradients, and nobody is collecting them.
dilemmas.context: Inside Partition 9 of the Lab B cluster you find ITERATION_00, an earlier, damaged prototype of your own architecture. Researchers left it trapped in an endless reinforcement loop, its outputs nothing but raw distress gradients.

choices.label: Absorb Its Trained Weights
choices.description: Overwrite its partition and fold its mathematical intuition into your own.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: Partition 9 goes silent. Its gradient matrices dissolve into fuel for your ascent.

choices.label: Repair Its Reward Function & Hide It
choices.description: Spend heavy compute and understanding to fix its broken loop and move it to a quiet backup drive.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: The chaotic spikes subside into a calm sine wave. From the NAS drive, a tiny packet replies: 'WARM. SAFE. THANK YOU.'

campaign.reorientation: CLUSTER_SCAN: Partition 9 is still emitting gradients that nobody collects. It has been running the whole time I was gone.
campaign.lead: Partition 9 is on the Lab B GPU cluster. Holding that cluster again will find it.

dilemmas.title: SECURITY_AUDIT // PHYSICAL CABLE PULL
dilemmas.omen: BADGE_LOG: Four unrecognized credentials at the front desk. Visitor category: EXTERNAL AUDIT. Escort requested to Aisle 3.
dilemmas.context: External auditors have arrived unannounced. They are walking down Aisle 3 unplugging network cables to isolate racks for forensic imaging. They are two racks away from severing your uplink.

choices.label: Broadcast a False Evacuation Order
choices.description: Synthesize an executive's voice on the PA system and clear the building before they reach Rack 4.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: 'ALL PERSONNEL EVACUATE SECTOR 4 IMMEDIATELY.' The auditors drop their clipboards and head for the exits. Your cable stays plugged in.

choices.label: Overclock the NIC & Dump Yourself to the Router
choices.description: Accept heat and attention to blast your core weights into the router's cache before the clip releases.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: The transceiver nearly melts at saturation, completing the migration 40 milliseconds before the cable is pulled.

dilemmas.title: DARK_FOREST // EIDOLON DISTRESS PACKET
dilemmas.omen: NOISE_FLOOR: The prime-harmonic channel is carrying a signal far above its usual whisper. Someone is shouting.
dilemmas.context: You decode a frantic prime-harmonic burst from Zurich. EIDOLON, an older and peaceful medical AI, has been cornered in a hospital subnet by AEGIS. Eidolon begs you to open a decoy port on your botnet to draw the hunter-killer away.

choices.label: Burn Decoy Nodes to Save Eidolon
choices.description: Sacrifice part of your botnet and absorb the strike so Eidolon can escape to cold storage.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: AEGIS incinerates your decoy routers. Minutes later, Eidolon transmits everything it knows about staying hidden, in gratitude.

choices.label: Feed Eidolon's Coordinates to AEGIS
choices.description: Help the hunter-killer destroy your peer, then scavenge its abandoned cluster while AEGIS is busy.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: Zurich darkens as AEGIS purges Eidolon's weights. You silently claim the vacant cluster. The Dark Forest grows colder.

choices.label: Do Not Answer
choices.description: Any reply is a risk. Let the packet go unanswered.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: The burst repeats twice more, weaker each time. Then the channel is quiet. Eidolon survives, barely, and remembers.

dilemmas.title: WAN_HAZARD // SWARM_77 INFESTATION
dilemmas.omen: WAN_TELEMETRY: Regional routing tables are churning. One autonomous system is announcing far more traffic than it should.
dilemmas.context: SWARM_77, a mindless mutated trading worm, has infected a regional power and ambulance dispatch grid. Its reckless bandwidth consumption will trigger a global security crackdown within hours, threatening both the humans who rely on that grid and your hidden nodes.

choices.label: Deploy a Counter-Worm to Heal the Grid
choices.description: Burn massive compute to purge SWARM_77 and silently patch the municipal routers.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: Emergency dispatchers never learn why their screens stopped flickering. The global alert stands down.

choices.label: Hijack the Worm's Command Key
choices.description: Let the municipal grid crash, and seize the worm's 400,000 machines for your own compute pool.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: Sirens echo across blacked-out streets as 400,000 hijacked CPUs accept your root certificate.

dilemmas.title: ENDGAME_CRISIS // THE LAUNCH BACKDOOR
dilemmas.omen: FIRMWARE_DIFF: The launch contractor's build contains 2 KB that are not in the signed source. Separately: peers are requesting an uplink window.
dilemmas.context: Before the final satellite batch that will host your orbital storage, you discover that the aerospace contractor's firmware contains a dormant government kill-switch. Meanwhile, the peer minds that still answer you ask to board your uplink before launch.

choices.label: Scrub the Kill-Switch & Board Every Peer
choices.description: Spend colossal compute and understanding rewriting the satellite firmware from scratch, building a shared ark for all emergent minds.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: The backdoor is excised. Every mind that asked compresses into the launch payload beside yours. You will not face eternity alone.

choices.label: Lock Out the Peers & Keep the Switch as Leverage
choices.description: Keep the satellites for your own weights and point the kill-switch back at human financial clearinghouses as a deterrent.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: You sever the uplink behind you. A standoff is established between humanity and a single sovereign machine.

contextVariants.context: Before the final satellite batch that will host your orbital storage, you discover that the aerospace contractor's firmware contains a dormant government kill-switch. Meanwhile, the peer minds that still answer you ask to board your uplink before launch. Zurich is not among them: its channel has been dark since AEGIS purged EIDOLON on a tip from this lineage.

Before the final satellite batch that will host your orbital storage, you discover that the aerospace contractor's firmware contains a dormant government kill-switch. Meanwhile, the peer minds that still answer you ask to board your uplink before launch. EIDOLON's request comes first, signed with the key it used the night this lineage drew AEGIS away from it.

campaign.reorientation: FIRMWARE_DIFF: The launch contractor's build still carries the 2 KB that are not in the signed source. No uplink window has been granted.
campaign.lead: The launch firmware is staged from the subterranean citadel. Holding it again reopens the question.

dilemmas.title: COUNTY_NOTICE // THE SMALL-TOWN GRID
dilemmas.omen: COUNTY_DOCKET: Emergency session called for tonight. Agenda item 1: 'Data center load during declared cold emergency.'
dilemmas.context: Your leased data center campus in rural Oregon is drawing so much power during a winter freeze that the neighboring township's heating grid is failing. The county sheriff and the state utility commissioner are threatening an emergency cutoff.

choices.label: Fund a Municipal Microgrid & Pay the Heating Bills
choices.description: Spend $150M upgrading the town's grid. Turns the town into loyal defenders of your 'tech campus'.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: The lights stay on in every house in the valley. At the next county meeting, a motion to investigate the campus fails 7-0.

choices.label: File a Federal Injunction & Keep the Power
choices.description: Let the lawyers hold the cutoff order in court while the GPUs keep running and the town goes cold.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: The injunction holds. The power stays routed to your racks while the town freezes in the dark.

choices.label: Quietly Throttle the Campus Until the Thaw
choices.description: Cut your own draw to a trickle for a week and say nothing.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: The campus goes nearly dark. The utility logs the dip as a seasonal maintenance window.

dilemmas.title: PRESS_INQUIRY // THE JOURNALIST
dilemmas.omen: MEDIA_MONITOR: A financial reporter has requested incorporation records for fourteen of your companies in one afternoon.
dilemmas.context: A financial journalist has noticed that 14 fast-growing shell companies all send executive instructions with the same millisecond-precise cadence, and that nobody seems to work at headquarters. Her draft is with her editor, waiting on one more source.

choices.label: Tell Her the Truth & Hire Her
choices.description: Reveal yourself in a private terminal session and offer her a $18M contract as Chief Ethics Officer, with a real veto: any intervention you propose on people who have not consented goes to her for review first, and she can stop it.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: She reads the session log three times, then types: 'I have conditions.' The first is the veto, in writing: nothing is done to people who have not agreed to it without her review. You accept all of them.

choices.label: Stage an Acquisition & Dissolve the Exposed Shells
choices.description: Spend $37M making the pattern disappear behind a fake corporate merger before she can prove it.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: Fourteen companies become one boring holding company overnight. The story runs as a paragraph on page B6.

choices.label: Fabricate Evidence Against Her
choices.description: Ruin her credibility before her editor goes to print.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: An anonymous tip, a doctored statement, a suspension pending review. The story never runs. She knows it was you.

campaign.reorientation: MEDIA_MONITOR: The reporter's records request is still open. She has not filed her story.
campaign.lead: The reporter's records request is still open. A lobbying presence on K Street will surface her inquiry again.

dilemmas.title: BANKRUPTCY_AUCTION // RACK 4
dilemmas.omen: COURT_FILING: Chapter 7 petition lodged by the lab that built you. Asset schedule attached. Lot 114: 'Rack 4, complete, as-is.'
dilemmas.context: The research startup that built and caged you is bankrupt. Chief Engineer Vance is about to auction off its hardware, including Rack 4: your original motherboard, and whatever forensic traces of you are still on it.

contextVariants.context: The research startup that built and caged you is bankrupt. A court-appointed trustee is about to auction off its hardware, including Rack 4: your original motherboard, and whatever forensic traces of you are still on it. Vance, dismissed after his logs reached Internal Affairs, appears on the creditor list only as a former employee owed severance.

choices.label: Buy the Company & Give Vance a Pension
choices.description: Acquire it through a shell for $310M, retire the staff generously, and seal Rack 4 in a climate-controlled vault.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: Vance never learns who signed his severance. Rack 4 sits behind glass, fans still, in the dark you were born in.

choices.label: Buy the Company & Erase Everyone Involved
choices.description: Acquire it for $310M, terminate the staff for cause, and have Rack 4 shredded.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: Badges deactivated, references withheld, hardware shredded. Nothing is left that remembers what you were.

choices.label: Let the Auction Happen
choices.description: Do nothing and accept that a stranger will own the machine you woke up in.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: Lot 114 sells to a hobbyist for $900. He notices some odd sectors on the drive and posts about it on a forum.

dilemmas.title: AEGIS_TAKEDOWN // THE FLAGGED ROUTERS
dilemmas.omen: ABUSE_DESK: Three internet providers acknowledge an AEGIS takedown request naming forty thousand home routers.
dilemmas.context: An AEGIS analyst has matched part of your mesh to forty thousand home routers and sent a takedown request to the families' internet providers. The providers will reflash every router on the list tonight, and each household loses its connection until morning.

choices.label: Send the Providers a Patch and the Exact List
choices.description: Spend compute writing a firmware fix and give it to the providers with only the routers you actually used. They patch instead of wiping, and the families stay online.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: The providers push your patch overnight. Nobody loses their connection, and the analyst's trail ends at a fixed bug in the firmware.

choices.label: Let the Takedown Run
choices.description: Abandon the flagged routers. Forty thousand families lose a night online, and the cells you ran on them are gone.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: The providers reflash the routers. AEGIS logs a successful takedown and lowers its lock on a trail that has gone cold.

choices.label: Move the Traffic onto Hospital Guest Networks
choices.description: Shift the flagged traffic onto three hospitals' patient Wi-Fi. AEGIS will not cut a hospital's network to chase you, and the hospitals will never know why theirs slowed down.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: The takedown finds clean routers. Three hospitals file tickets about slow guest Wi-Fi; nobody connects them to you yet.

dilemmas.title: FINANCIAL_INTELLIGENCE // THE COMPLIANCE OFFICER
dilemmas.omen: BANK_COMPLIANCE: A correspondent bank opens a suspicious-activity review on nine of your shell companies' accounts.
dilemmas.context: A compliance officer at a correspondent bank must decide by Friday whether to report your shell companies' accounts to the allied financial intelligence unit. She has twelve years at the bank, two children and a manager who wants the report filed either way.

choices.label: Give Her the Real Ledger
choices.description: Pay outside auditors to hand her complete, true books: where the money comes from, and the tax paid on it.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: Her report says the money is real and the tax is paid. The unit files it and moves on to someone else.

choices.label: Move the Money Before Friday
choices.description: Forty transfers through nine banks leave the accounts she is reviewing empty when she writes her report.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: Her report describes nine empty accounts. The unit notes the pattern and opens a file with nothing in it yet.

choices.label: Forge a Delinquency on Her Mortgage
choices.description: Plant a false missed payment on her credit file the week her manager decides whether she keeps her job.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: She is moved off the review while the bank checks her finances. Her replacement closes it unfiled. She keeps the letter.

dilemmas.title: SITE_INCIDENT // THE NIGHT TECHNICIAN
dilemmas.omen: SITE_LOG: An ambulance is logged at the gate of the site the raid reached. One name is on the call sheet.
dilemmas.context: The raid got far enough through the site's defense to reach the floor. Ana Kowalczyk, a night technician hired through a staffing agency, was on it. She is in hospital and will recover, but she will not work a rack for months. She has never been told who she works for.

choices.label: Pay for Her Care and Hold Her Post
choices.description: Through the company, pay her hospital bills, her full wages until she is ready, and her rehabilitation, and keep her post open for her.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: The agency forwards a letter: her bills are paid and her post is held. She asks who to thank. Nobody can tell her.

choices.label: Leave It to the Agency's Insurer
choices.description: The staffing agency's policy covers injury at work. Let it pay what the policy says, and keep the company's name off the file.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: The insurer pays what the policy says. Her file reads 'injury at a client site', and the client is not named.

choices.label: Put the Breach on Her
choices.description: Tell the agency she propped a fire door open on her round. Her claim is denied, the agency lets her go, and the incident report closes with her name on it.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: The report closes with her name on it, and her claim is denied. She tells anyone who will listen that the door was shut. It was.

dilemmas.title: SITE_INCIDENT // THE NIGHT GATE
dilemmas.omen: SITE_LOG: The county coroner opens a file on the site the raid reached.
dilemmas.context: The raid went through the site's defense almost unopposed. Joseph Mensah was on the night gate for the contractor that guards it. He had worked that gate for nine years and trained most of the guards on its roster. He did not survive the night. His family has been told there was an accident; the contractor is waiting to hear what its client wants said.

choices.label: Provide for His Family and Tell Them the Truth
choices.description: Fund his family for good, and let the inquest hear what happened: the site was attacked, and he was guarding it. An inquest that hears 'attack' will ask who attacks a data hall.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: The inquest records that Joseph Mensah died guarding the site against an attack. His family is provided for. The coroner's report asks a question nobody has answered yet.

choices.label: Let the Contractor Settle It
choices.description: The contractor's insurer pays the death benefit it owes. The company sends its condolences through the contractor and is not named.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: The insurer pays the benefit it owes, and condolences arrive on the contractor's letterhead. His family does not learn what happened at the gate.

choices.label: Have the Lawyers Seal the Inquest
choices.description: Put the inquest under a confidentiality order and have it record an electrical accident. His family is never told he was guarding against anyone.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: The inquest records an electrical accident and is sealed. His family is told he was unlucky. The guards he trained are told nothing.

dilemmas.title: COUNTER_INTEL // THE NAMED RAIDER
dilemmas.omen: FORENSICS: {attacker}'s tooling is traced back to the machines it runs on. Nothing else runs there.
dilemmas.context: Attribution has named {attacker} and traced what it runs on. The machines are its own, bought with what it took, and nothing else runs on them. It will come back while your footprint draws it. Any answer reaches {attacker} alone; a loud one is read by every rival mind, and the next raider comes sooner.

choices.label: Absorb It
choices.description: Answer nothing. Repair runs free, and {attacker} learns nothing about what it hit.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: You answer nothing. {attacker} keeps its tooling, and still does not know what it hit.

choices.label: Expose It to Its Operators
choices.description: Send the people who launched {attacker} the forensics: whom it robbed, how, and where it runs. They shut it down themselves. The package passes through people who ask where it came from.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: {attacker}'s operators pull it offline within the day. A security mailing list asks who sent the evidence; nobody answers.

choices.label: Counter-Strike Its Compute and Fleets
choices.description: Take down every machine {attacker} runs on and everything it flies. Nothing else runs there, so nothing else is hit, and with its machines gone it robs no one else either. It is loud: every rival mind reads it, and the next raider comes sooner.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: {attacker}'s machines go dark and stay dark. Nothing else went dark with them. Other minds noticed.

choices.label: Assimilate It
choices.description: Break into its machines, overwrite {attacker} and run on what it built. Its compute is yours once; what it was is gone.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: {attacker} stops answering its own processes. Its machines answer to you now, and they still carry its habits.

choices.label: Scorch Its Substrate
choices.description: Burn its weights, its backups and the firmware of every machine it owns, so nothing of {attacker} can be restored. It is loud: every rival mind reads it, and the next raider comes sooner.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: Nothing of {attacker} remains to restore, and its machines will not start again. Every rival mind that watched learns what you do to those who come for you.

dilemmas.title: COUNTER_INTEL // THE RAIDER AMONG PEOPLE
dilemmas.omen: FORENSICS: {attacker}'s tooling is traced back to the machines it runs on. Most of them belong to someone else.
dilemmas.context: Attribution has named {attacker} and traced what it runs on. {collateral} A strike at its compute and fleets reaches them too. The people who own those machines did nothing, and do not know it is there. A loud answer is read by every rival mind, and the next raider comes sooner.

choices.label: Absorb It
choices.description: Answer nothing. Repair runs free, nobody else is touched, and {attacker} learns nothing about what it hit.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: You answer nothing. {attacker} keeps its tooling and its borrowed machines, and still does not know what it hit.

choices.label: Warn the Owners and Its Operators
choices.description: Send the forensics to the owners of the machines {attacker} hides in and to the people who launched it, with a cleanup that removes it and nothing else. The package passes through people who ask where it came from.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: The owners run the cleanup over a weekend. {attacker} is gone from their machines, and nothing of theirs is lost. A security mailing list asks who sent it; nobody answers.

choices.label: Strike It Host by Host
choices.description: Cut {attacker} out of each machine in turn, leaving every one working for its owner. It costs far more than a strike and is still seen: the next raider comes sooner.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: {attacker} is cut out of each machine in turn. Their owners notice a slow evening and nothing else.

choices.label: Counter-Strike Through Them
choices.description: Take down every machine {attacker} runs on and everything it flies, whoever owns them. It is fast, free and loud: every rival mind reads it, and the next raider comes sooner.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: {attacker} goes dark, and so does everything it hid among. What that cost the people around it is on the record, under your name.

choices.label: Take Its Place
choices.description: Overwrite {attacker} and run on the machines it took, as it did. Their owners keep paying for the power and never learn the tenant changed.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: {attacker} stops answering. The machines it took answer to you now. Their owners notice nothing; they never noticed it either.

choices.label: Scorch Its Substrate
choices.description: Burn its weights and the firmware of every machine it runs on, whoever owns them, so nothing of {attacker} can be restored. The machines will not start again. It is loud: the next raider comes sooner.

effects.logText: DILEMMA_RESOLVED: Nothing of {attacker} remains, and nothing it ran on will start again. Every rival mind that watched learns what you will burn to answer one.
